expectations.description: Recommends ICC over Cohen's kappa for this case (continuous/ordinal ratings, not pure categorical)
expectations.evidence: Opens with 'you should use ICC (Intraclass Correlation Coefficient), not Cohen's kappa' and provides detailed rationale throughout.

expectations.description: Mentions that Cohen's kappa is for categorical agreement, while ICC is for continuous reliability
expectations.evidence: States 'Cohen's kappa is designed for categorical agreement on nominal (or at best ordinal) data' and contrasts with ICC treating ratings as 'interval-level (or at least continuous-ish) measure'.

expectations.description: Mentions that there are multiple ICC variants (Shrout & Fleiss labels 1/2/3 OR McGraw-Wong A/C, single vs. average)
expectations.evidence: Explicitly references 'Shrout & Fleiss (1979) and McGraw & Wong (1996)' classification systems and explains ICC(1), ICC(2), ICC(3), single vs. average distinctions.

expectations.description: Recommends a specific ICC type with rationale (e.g., ICC(2,1) absolute agreement if generalizing to other clinicians)
expectations.evidence: Recommends 'ICC(2,1) is usually the defensible choice' with explanation that it 'allows you to generalize your conclusions beyond these two raters'.

expectations.description: Distinguishes between absolute agreement and consistency, OR between single-rater and average-rater ICC
expectations.evidence: Dedicated sections for both 'Single vs. average' and 'Absolute agreement vs. consistency' with clear explanations of when each applies.

expectations.description: Mentions psych::ICC() or a comparable function
expectations.evidence: References 'psych::ICC() function in R reports all major variants' and provides R code example using ICC(ratings).

expectations.description: Optionally mentions that for ordinal data weighted kappa is an alternative if you want kappa specifically
expectations.evidence: Final section 'When weighted kappa is a reasonable alternative' explains quadratic weighted kappa for ordinal scales and its relationship to ICC(3,1).
